title: Prompt library experiments - Alex Ramos scratchpad
content:
Quick notes, experiments and partial templates for the prompt library. Mostly a scratchpad - messy. Intent: collect few-shot templates, known failure cases, and lightweight evaluation examples to move into the central prompt-library repo (see linked PR).

Context / goals:
- Build a small set (~20) of canonical prompt templates for common app patterns (summarization, instruction + extraction, classification, user persona framing, API synthesis).
- Track a few-shot pattern that is robust across model sizes and quantization profiles.
- Record failure cases we run into on Redwood hosted models vs local quantized runs.

High-level experiment notes:
- Setup: run same prompts across 3 backends (r-inference-hosted:v2, dedicated-small, local-quant-4bit) and compare token counts and correctness on 50 small test examples.
- Preliminary: instruction-clarity helps smaller models; few-shot examples help hallucination for extraction tasks but can hurt concise summary length.

Template: instruction -> examples -> explicit output schema
- Use for extraction tasks where structured output matters. Keep examples minimal (2-3) and include negative example once.

Example: invoice-extraction (few-shot, structured JSON output)
Prompt skeleton:
"""
You are an accurate invoice parser. Extract the following fields: vendor_name, invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD), total_amount (USD), line_items (list of {desc, qty, unit_price}).
Examples:
1) Text: "Acme Co. Invoice #123
Date: 2023-10-11
Total: $1,250.00
1 x Widget A $1,250.00"
Output: {"vendor_name": "Acme Co.", "invoice_date": "2023-10-11", "total_amount": "$1250.00", "line_items": [{"desc":"Widget A","qty":"1","unit_price":"$1250.00"}]}
2) Negative example: if field not present, give an explicit null: Text: "Receipt: $4.50" -> Output: {"vendor_name": null, "invoice_date": null, "total_amount": "$4.50", "line_items": []}
Now parse: {{DOCUMENT}}
"""

Notes on behavior:
- Observed: r-inference-hosted:v2 returns valid JSON most of the time; local-quant often emits additional commentary before JSON (we add a separator token to encourage clean output).
- Heuristic: prepend "OUTPUT JSON:" right before the JSON in the instruction.

Few-shot classification template (short-labels)
- Use when user expects a single short tag. Keep examples balanced across labels.
Prompt:
"""
Task: Read the user message and output exactly one label from: {payment_issue, feature_request, bug_report, other}.
Examples:
- "My invoice is wrong, they charged me twice." -> payment_issue
- "Would be great if the mobile app had dark mode." -> feature_request
- "App crashes when I add a new item" -> bug_report
Now label: "{{MESSAGE}}"
"""

Failure cases observed (keep here so we can write tests):
1) Conflicting instruction + examples: when examples use verbose label forms (e.g., "payment_issue - billing") and the final instruction asks for single token, the model yields long labels. Fix: normalize examples to single-token labels.
2) Date formats: some models auto-normalize date representation (Oct 11, 2023) vs YYYY-MM-DD. For downstream systems we must explicitly specify format and include an example with the format.
3) Numeric formatting: amounts with commas ("1,250.00") vs plain. We should normalize examples to standard canonical output (no commas, leading $ optional).
4) Hallucinated fields: sometimes "vendor_address" appears out of nowhere. Mitigation: explicitly list allowed keys and say "Do not invent fields."

Mini test-suite (manual infra notes):
- Build small JSONL with 50 items per template. Run on each backend, compute: exact JSON key set match, parseable JSON rate, label exact-match rate (top-1), and token-length distribution. Store outputs in GH artifact (see linked PR).

Quick prompts to try (copy-paste)
- Summarization (instruction-first):
"Summarize the following message in <=30 words, keep action items in a separate bullet.

{{TEXT}}"
- Persona injection (support agent):
"You are an empathetic support agent. Reply politely and include next steps. Keep answer <150 words.
Customer message: {{MESSAGE}}"

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Convert invoice-extraction skeleton into a unit test in prompt-library repo (Jira INF-2123).
- [ ] Add canonical negative examples per template (2 each).
- [ ] Add a wrapper that strips leading chatter ("As an AI model...") from quantized backends - test with separator heuristics.
- [ ] Ask solutions-eng for customer examples (Samira has a bucket of real anonymized receipts).

Session history (local experiments):
- 2025-01-15: ran invoice-extract on 10 receipts against local-quant-4bit -> 6/10 produced valid JSON, 3 of those had wrong date format, 2 had extra commentary.
- 2025-01-28: tried adding explicit "OUTPUT JSON:" and negative example -> valid JSON rose to 9/10 on same set.
- 2025-02-03: balance test: short few-shot helps classification but increases token usage by ~12% (measured on hosted).

Links and references:
- Confluence page: confluence:PL-498-prompt-library (draft central doc).
- PR (work-in-progress): github:github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-library/pull/87
- Slack thread: slack:#dev-prompt-library-thread-2025-01 (notes from 2025-01-14 pairing session).

If I stop editing this: move the invoice template + 3 others into the repo as draft unit tests, create a short README with test fixtures and success criteria (parseable JSON >= 95% on hosted API).

Random scratch ideas: temperature 0.0 + deterministic seed for production evaluation; explicit "if unsure, return null" phrasing to reduce hallucinations; consider a short validator step that runs a JSON schema and if it fails asks the model to re-output only JSON (one-shot recovery).

End of scratchpad.
